sn13.3:1.2: Also at [sn56.53](). | Yamunā is a major southern tributary of the Ganges, joining it at Payāga. | Aciravatī is today the West Rapti, on whose banks Sāvatthī was located. Sarabhū (Sanskrit _sarayū_) is the modern Gaghara, one of the largest northern tributaries of the Ganges, joining it west of Pāṭaliputta. | Mahī is the modern Kosi, which flows from Tibet through Nepal to join the Ganges in Aṅga, east of Pāṭaliputta around modern Kursela.
